title: Cycle Tracer: scenario library & scope-liquidation playbook
creator: Priya Kaur
description:
Problem: We frequently run into mid-cycle overcommit where critical path work is blocked by staffing volatility and late scope additions. Existing cycle playbooks are a mix of tribal knowledge; teams request clearer, scenario-driven guidance for when to trim scope, shift engineers between lanes, or trigger surge lanes.

Goal: Produce a compact, repeatable 'Cycle Tracer' playbook (scenario library + decision matrix + templated communications) that PMs and Eng leads can use to make consistent staffing and scope-liquidation decisions. The playbook should reduce decision latency, surface measurable trade-offs, and integrate signals from Console usage dashboards and team capacity charts.

Success metrics: (1) Reduce average time-to-decision for scope-trim events from 28h -> <8h; (2) Decrease mid-cycle overcommit frequency by 20% for Q2 cycles where playbook is used; (3) 80% adoption by PMs for at least two planning cycles.

Scope: Deliver a scenario catalog (common failure modes and recommended actions), a scoring rubric (impact / effort / customer exposure), a staffed-rotation protocol, and ready-to-send stakeholder templates. Include a set of automation hooks (dashboard links and a GitHub issue template) but do not build automated staffing reassignment tooling in this ticket.

Out of scope: Full integration with payroll/roster systems or automated hire/contractor provisioning.

Stakeholders: Product (Priya Kaur), Eng leads (Liam O'Connor, Marta Ruiz), Design (Ava Chen for comms), SRE (for capacity signals), People Ops (for staffing constraints).
acceptance_criteria: A concise scenario library (>= 8 scenarios) published to Confluence with examples and one annotated case study
Decision matrix template that outputs recommended actions (keep/block/trim/swap/borrow) when filled
Two stakeholder communication templates (urgent trim, planned scope pause) in Drive
A lightweight dashboard panel bookmarked linking cycle capacity signals and active PRs
Runbook reviewed and approved by at least two Eng leads and one PM in a cross-functional review meeting
